children: With bitcoin (BTC-US) remaining more or less stagnant over the week, trading at $84.4K late Friday afternoon, compared with $84.1K at on Sept. 25, crypto and blockchain-related stocks accounted for four of the five biggest financial decliners of the past week.

Three of the biggest gainers were Brazilian banks ahead of the first round of the country's presidential election on Sunday. The winner of the final round, which is set for later in the month, will get to fill vacancies in Brazil's Supreme Court, central bank, and economic regulators.
For the week, the State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF
slipped 2.5% as Treasury yields continued to climb, underperforming the S&P 500's (
) 0.3% dip. For the past month, it dropped 7.3% compared with the S&P's 0.1% increase.
The decliners were led by Riot Platforms'
14% drop for the week, followed by blockchain-focused firm Figure Technology's
11% decline.

Stablecoin issuer Circle Internet

On the opposite side of the performance spectrum, Virtu Financial
scored the biggest gain of the week, rising 10%. Early in the week, it announced the launch of a block-trading indications network for equity securities listed on the Saudi Exchange.
Brazilian banks took the next three spots, with Inter & Co.
rising 7.2%, Banco Bradesco
gaining 7.0%, and Itaú Unibanco Holding
climbing 5.9%.
HCI Group
, a property & casualty insurance business, rounded out the top five with a 5.3% increase for the week.
